what.text: Phentolamine is an alpha-adrenergic blocker: it blocks the receptors that adrenaline-like signals use to tighten blood vessels, so vessels widen. FDA-approved products are an injection used around surgery for pheochromocytoma (an adrenaline-making tumour), OraVerse (a dental injection that speeds the end of mouth numbness) and Ryzumvi eye drops.

what.text: Why it was studied for erectile dysfunction

items.text: Tightening of penile arteries and smooth muscle appears to be mainly under alpha-adrenergic control. Blocking alpha-1 and alpha-2 receptors helped erections in animal and human lab models, according to a review by the oral drug's investigators.

items.text: For erectile dysfunction (ED), phentolamine has been injected into the penis in compounded mixes with papaverine, or with papaverine and alprostadil ("Trimix"). Two-drug mixes are called "Bimix" in some papers. A tablet, Vasomax, was tested by mouth. None of these is FDA approved for ED.

research.text: Phentolamine has been studied for ED in two ways: as a tablet (Vasomax) in placebo-controlled trials around 2000, and as part of injected mixes. The results below are from the published abstracts; the oral Phase 3 trials are known mainly through reviews by their investigators.

A 2001 review by investigators of the oral tablet describes two large placebo-controlled trials (ZON300 and ZON301) and two long-term open-label studies. It reports better IIEF erectile function scores and more successful penetration attempts than placebo, and side effects of stuffy nose (10%), headache (3%), dizziness (3%), fast heart rate (3%) and nausea (1%). Peak levels came 30 to 60 minutes after a dose; half-life was 5 to 7 hours. This is a review, not a trial report; the full trial papers were not read here.

research.title: Oral phentolamine vs sildenafil (Int J Impot Res 2002)

facts.v: Ugarte F, Hurtado-Coll A. Int J Impot Res 2002;14 Suppl 2:S48-53
open-label, multi-center; no placebo group
242 men with ED (119 phentolamine, 123 sildenafil)
oral phentolamine 40 mg or sildenafil 25 to 100 mg
8 weeks
IIEF questionnaire and two global questions

research.found: Successful intercourse was reported by 42% of men on phentolamine and 88% on sildenafil. Side effects (stuffy nose, headache, fast heart rate, nausea) were more frequent on phentolamine (41% vs 33%), except headache.

research.title: Oral phentolamine at bedtime and night-time erections (Int J Impot Res 2001)

facts.v: Hatzichristou DG, Apostolidis A, Tzortzis V, et al. Int J Impot Res 2001;13(5):303-8
double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover
5 men with mild to moderate ED (mean age 34.8)
oral phentolamine 40 mg or placebo before sleep, three nights each
night-time erections on a RigiScan monitor

research.found: The number of rigid night-time erections lasting 10 minutes or more rose on phentolamine (P = 0.02). No side effects were recorded. Only 5 men took part.

src.label: Hatzichristou et al., Int J Impot Res, PubMed

research.title: Papaverine plus phentolamine vs alprostadil (J Urol 1997)

facts.v: Bechara A, Casabé A, Chéliz G, et al. J Urol 1997;157(6):2132-4
randomized into 6 groups, each tested with both solutions and placebo, 1 week apart
60 men (mean age 58) with ED for more than 6 months, during erection testing
papaverine 30 mg plus phentolamine 0.5 mg, or alprostadil 30 micrograms, injected into the penis
single test injections
erection good enough for penetration; short-term side effects

research.found: 54% responded to papaverine plus phentolamine and 50% to alprostadil (not significantly different). Prolonged erection occurred in 18% and 15%. Pain was reported by 15% and 35% (P < 0.05).

research.title: Trimix doses vs alprostadil alone (Int J Impot Res 2005)

facts.v: Seyam R, Mohamed K, Akhras AA, Rashwan H. Int J Impot Res 2005;17(4):346-53
prospective; 9 groups of Trimix doses; each man got alprostadil 20 micrograms and one Trimix dose, 1 week apart
180 men with ED; mean age 50.5
Trimix (phentolamine 1 mg, alprostadil 2.5 to 10 micrograms, papaverine 5 to 20 mg) vs alprostadil alone
two clinic visits
penile artery flow on ultrasound, rigidity, satisfaction, side effects

research.found: Blood flow, rigidity, pain and satisfaction did not differ significantly. Trimix gave longer erections and more priapism than alprostadil alone.

research.title: Reversing lip and tongue numbness after dental work (JADA 2008)

facts.v: Hersh EV, Moore PA, Papas AS, et al. J Am Dent Assoc 2008;139(8):1080-93
two multicenter, randomized, double-blinded, controlled trials vs a sham injection
484 adolescents and adults having fillings or scaling with a local anaesthetic containing a vasoconstrictor
phentolamine mesylate or a sham injection at the same site after the procedure
5 hours of follow-up
time to normal lip and tongue sensation, and function

research.found: Median recovery of the lower lip was 70 minutes with phentolamine vs 155 minutes with sham; tongue 60 vs 125 minutes; upper lip 50 vs 133 minutes (P < 0.0001).

us.text: Phentolamine is FDA approved, by prescription, for pheochromocytoma (Regitine, 1952, and generics), dental numbness reversal (OraVerse, 2008) and eye uses (Ryzumvi, 2023). It is not approved for ED, so use for ED is off-label. Compounded Bimix and Trimix are not FDA approved. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: Regitine was approved January 30, 1952 (NDA 008278) and is now discontinued; generic injections remain. Approved uses: preventing or controlling high blood pressure episodes from pheochromocytoma around surgery, preventing or treating skin damage after norepinephrine leaks from a vein, and the phentolamine test for pheochromocytoma.

world.lead: Phentolamine is an approved prescription medicine in the US and Canada, for uses other than ED. Its status in the UK, the EU and Australia was not confirmed. No regulator record found here lists ED as an approved use. It is not on WADA's Prohibited List.

after.text: Phentolamine is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. It is not in the 2027 Monitoring Program either. Class S0 covers only substances with no current government approval for human therapeutic use, and phentolamine is approved for some use (see above).

side.text: The injection label warns of heart attack and stroke-like events, usually with steep drops in blood pressure, and of fast heart rate and rhythm problems. Injected into the penis in mixes, it adds to the risk of prolonged erection and priapism.

items.text: heart attack, spasm and blockage of brain arteries have been reported after phentolamine, usually with marked low blood pressure. It must not be used after a heart attack or with angina or other coronary artery disease.
